newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Juppe down in French opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Juppe down in French opinion poll.

text.p: Public support for Prime Minister Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe has slipped to new lows, according to an opinion poll taken even before the start of a crippling strike by French truckers.

The CSA survey for the weekly La Vie released on Tuesday indicated that just 37 percent of those polled trusted Chirac to tackle France's main problems, against 38 percent in a similar poll last month.

Juppe's rating slipped three points to 28 percent in the survey of 1,010 people taken on November 12 and 13, before the start of a strike by French truckers. The strike, now in its ninth day, is strangling France with blockades on highways.
Other surveys show that the truckers have wide support for their demands, including higher wages, shorter hours and retirement at 55 instead of 60.

The poll said 53 percent of those questioned expressed no confidence in Chirac and 62 percent lacked confidence in Juppe, widely blamed for rising unemployment, sluggish economic growth and budget austerity.
